Wolf 93 begins mating with daughter in 2002; inbreeding rises again
From 2002: moose aerial survey method replaces reconstruction for estimates

Moose begins very slow recovery. Active beaver sites: 92 (wolves killed many beavers). Fox index monitoring ongoing
Winter ticks peaked 2007. Wolf inbreeding worsening. LSTV spinal deformity rate: >80% by late 1990s
Wolf population decline begins April 2009. Parvovirus/adenovirus antibodies detected in wolves
Wolf rapid decline 24->19. Inbreeding depression increasingly affecting survival/reproduction
Wolf decline continues: 19->16. Mine pit drowning killed 3 wolves 2011-2012
Wolf declined to 9 (62% decline since 2009). Predation rate 3.3% (low). Zero recruitment. Moose recovering

WOLF ALL-TIME LOW (8). First year with zero pup production in project history. Kill rate 1.3 moose/wolf/month (near record high due to 122 moose/wolf ratio). Predation rate 2.4% (record low). Moose calf 21% (near record high). Moose mortality 11%. Snow depth 30cm (below avg 44cm). Active beaver sites 168 (69% increase since 2010 as wolf predation dropped)
Wolf population remains critically low. Moose continues recovery toward long-term average
Wolf at existential crisis level (3). 2 packs became 1 group. NPS begins planning wolf translocation under Endangered Species Act
Only 2 non-reproducing wolves remain. Island essentially without wolf predation. Moose browsing on balsam fir remains low. Balsam fir sapling height growth ~20cm/yr (healthy - low browsing)
2 non-reproducing wolves. Moose density rising rapidly -> increasing balsam fir browse pressure. Balsam fir growth ~20cm (still relatively healthy)
NPS wolf translocation authorized. 2 remaining wolves (both old). Browse pressure: <20% of fir saplings browsed. Balsam fir growth ~18cm

19 wolves translocated by NPS (Sept 2018-March 2019): 4 from Minnesota; 3 from mainland Ontario; 8 from Michipicoten Island; then 4 from Michigan Sept 2019. 1 litter born April 2019. Wolf count 14 by March 2019. MOOSE PEAK (~2060). Balsam fir browse: ~80% of saplings terminally browsed (alarming high)

Wolf: likely 12 possibly 14 (furtive behavior; aircraft avoidance). 4 social groups. Moose declined 9% (2060->1876). Predation rate 4.5% (below avg). Balsam fir terminal browse ~80% saplings. 25 moose GPS-collared March 2020
NO WINTER SURVEY - COVID-19 pandemic prevented all winter fieldwork. Summer fieldwork continued. Two litters born 2020 confirmed

Wolf population doubled (12->28) over 2 years. 2 main packs (East 13+ wolves; West 13+ wolves). 2 litters born April 2020; 2 litters born April 2021. Predation rate 8.7% (highest since 2011). Moose declined 28% (1876->1346). Malnutrition important cause of moose death 2019-2022. 19 moose GPS-collared Feb 2022

3 packs: East(11 wolves incl 12M); West(5 wolves incl 7M); others(~15). 3 possibly 4 litters born April 2022 (first time 4 litters since ~2002). Wolf recruitment 25% (similar to long-term avg 28%). Wolf survival 86% (above long-term avg 74%). Kill rate 0.52 moose/wolf/month (below long-term avg 0.70). Predation rate 10% (at long-term avg). Moose calves 1.7% (VERY LOW vs avg 13%). 26 moose killed by wolves in 49 days. Moose declined 28% (1346->967). Fox abundance index 20.3

4 packs for first time since 2011: West(4+); Middle(7+); East(13+); Northeast(5+). Moose calves <6% (5.5%; low vs avg 13%). Moose declined 13% (967->840). Study ended early due to unseasonably warm weather. Balsam fir sapling height growth 3.5cm (near record low; was 18-20cm in healthy years). Hare index 4.39. Wolf predation: 86-92% of moose deaths attributed to wolves

NO WINTER SURVEY - aviation resources unexpectedly unavailable shortly before start of season. Summer fieldwork continued. Balsam fir sapling height growth 3.5cm (still at record low). Sapling survival <80% (also record low). Tick burden: avg 57% hair loss (close to long-term avg 51%). Some moose had 98% hair damage. 115 moose discovered; 86% killed by wolves. Two adult bulls found dead with antlers locked (only 4th such occurrence in 65+ years)

WOLF NEAR-HISTORIC HIGH (37 wolves; highest since 1979). 524 moose (approaching all-time low 385 in 2006). 3 packs: West(13 wolves); East(12 wolves); Northeast(12 wolves). All 3 packs raised pups summer 2025; all showed courtship/breeding Feb 2026. ZERO CALVES observed during census - FIRST TIME IN 68-YEAR HISTORY. Kill rate 0.56 moose/wolf/month. Predation rate 24% (ONE OF HIGHEST EVER; avg=10%). 28 moose killed by wolves in 41 days. 88% of annual moose deaths from wolf predation. Balsam fir terminal browse rate: 4% of saplings (down from >80% in 2019-2021; showing decline in browsing pressure). Balsam fir height growth 2.7cm (RECORD LOW; expected ~20cm in healthy years). Fir trees have not recovered despite 4 years of lower browsing. Ice bridge formed connecting Isle Royale to mainland Jan-mid Feb 2026. Avg snow depth 56cm (above long-term avg 46.5cm). Avg temperature -8.3C. Ramsonde hardness 8.7 (low snowpack density). Fox abundance index 20.3. Hare index 3.9 hares/100km hiked. Otter tracks on 47 sq-mile sections (down from 83 in 2023). Wolf predation on otters observed for first time in winter
